title: Contain kernel exported symbols with namespacing & run rolling-compat stress suite
creator: Ava Kim
description: Reduce runtime instability caused by symbol collisions and non-deterministic kernel probing across mixed driver/CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS environments. Implement a linker-level namespacing strategy (symbol versioning + linker namespaces) to isolate third-party kernel bundles, add a lightweight compatibility-proxy that performs deterministic ordering and fallback selection, and stabilize CI with a rolling-compat stress test that exercises mixed driver versions, quantized kernels, and KV-cache warmups.
acceptance_criteria: All GPU kernel bundles are built with namespaced exported symbols; no duplicate global symbols in runtime process.
Compatibility proxy can route to fallback kernel variant when primary fails without requiring full process restart.
Rolling-compat stress test runs in CI matrix (driver 11.x/12.x/13.x, CUDA 11/12/13, Triton 2/3) and completes within configured SLO on staging pool.
No regression in nominal latency (median token latency +/-5%) across canary workloads.
Confluence design doc and Datadog dashboard linked; e2e runbook updated for on-call.
steps: Audit current kernel bundles to enumerate exported symbols and overlapping names.
Prototype linker namespace approach using GNU linker version scripts and symbol prefixing at build-time.
Implement compatibility-proxy binary that loads kernel bundles in isolation and exposes a stable C ABI.
Add deterministic probe ordering (staging -> canary pool -> fallback) and a retry policy for kernel init failures.
Compose rolling-compat stress suite and add to CI pipeline with multi-version driver matrix.
Run canary on dedicated GPU pool with telemetry and automatic rollback on SLA breach.
technical_notes: Prefer not to use LD_PRELOAD in production; go with linker symbol versioning and limited dlmopen separation where supported.
Cutlass kernels require symbol aliasing for outdated instantiations; post-link script will rewrite mangled names for conflicting objects.
Compatibility-proxy uses a thin grpc control plane for routing decisions and a local unix socket for high-perf RPC to runtime.
KV cache warmup is flakey under early-exit failures; add idempotent warmup with expiry to avoid stale entries after fallback.
risks: Driver incompatibilities that cannot be fully mitigated without kernel/driver updates on customer machines.
Increased binary size and marginal startup overhead due to probe wrapper and versioning metadata.
Edge cases where dlmopen is not available (older distribs) requiring fallbacks to process isolation.
